name: Séraphine Okonkwo-Delacroix
description: Séraphine Okonkwo-Delacroix is Meridian 88's most famous doping scandal, a French-Nigerian distance runner who competed in the Purist Circuit as an unaugmented athlete from 2205 to 2211 and won four consecutive Great Lakes championships before a routine tissue audit revealed latent geneware modifications — a suite of mitochondrial enhancements and myofibril density optimizations so precisely embedded in her baseline genome that three separate labs initially classified them as natural variation. The modifications were traced to a licensed geneware clinic that had accepted payment from an anonymous Tier 4 account. She has maintained since her 2211 disqualification that she did not know.
story_hooks: Okonkwo-Delacroix has spent four years quietly building her own case that the geneware was installed without her knowledge during what she was told was a standard sports medicine consultation — and she has found two other Purist athletes who had the same consultant and similar unexplained results.

The geneware modifications installed in her are a specific proprietary variant that only one lab in Meridian 88 is capable of producing — a lab that officially ceased operations in 2208 but whose equipment appears to have been relocated rather than decommissioned.

A Tier 1 runner who idolized Okonkwo-Delacroix before the scandal is now competing in the Purist Circuit and has been approached by the same anonymous Tier 4 account that the original investigation traced — this time with an offer rather than a covert modification.
